author: Allie Root
title: Officials work to find person who abandoned newborn puppies in Lexington - NewsBreak
text:
By Allie Root ,
2 hours ago
LEXINGTON, Ky. ( FOX 56 ) — Lexington officials are investigating a sad case of animal abandonment , trying to find the person responsible for leaving newborn puppies outside an apartment complex over the weekend. They told FOX 56 that criminal charges could be forthcoming.
It was outside the metropolitan apartments in Lexington where officials said two puppies were abandoned in a box Saturday night. They’re only about a week old.
LATEST KENTUCKY NEWS: “After we picked them up, they immediately went home with a staff member, and they were being bottle-fed every two hours,” said Cruelty Investigator Jai Hamilton. “Like, that is how much these newborns needed care.”
Hamilton said it’s a heartless act to leave puppies to fend for themselves with no ability to get their own shelter, food, or water. In this case, Hamilton said the puppies could have died if authorities didn’t intervene.
She noted that the person responsible could face charges. Abandonment of an animal is a misdemeanor that’s punishable by up to a year in jail.
“Anyone who has a disregard for life, whether it be puppies, you know, animals, other people, it’s just not fair to society, and it’s just not good for others,” said Hamilton.
LATEST KENTUCKY LISTS AND RANKINGS: Hamilton said animal abandonment seems to be on the rise. Right now, Lexington’s humane society and animal control are caring for more than 400 animals.
“It’s call after call- ‘I have to surrender my dog. I have to surrender my cat. I’m moving. I had a baby.’ So, it does get really overwhelming.”
If you are unable to care for an animal any longer, Hamilton urges you to reach out to family and friends first before turning to a shelter.
“It might have to be a couple of months until there is space for someone to take that animal, or you find the right fit for your animal. So, my advice is to be patient but do right by your pet.”
If you have information about who abandoned the two puppies, call Lexington-Fayette Animal Care and Control at 859-255-9033 extension 229.
